architecture.summary: Rise of Lyric is a lightweight HTML5 3D multiplayer game. This document describes the runtime foundation that has been built: server, client bootstrap, networking protocol, rendering pipeline, and project layout. No gameplay rules, art, or visual design have been implemented yet - this is boilerplate/plumbing only.

requirement.name: Browser
requirement.detail: any modern browser with WebGL2 and WebSocket support

runtime.dependencies: Zero external npm dependencies on the server. The client vendors Three.js as a static local file (no CDN, no bundler, no build step required).

var.name: DEBUG
var.detail: set to any value to enable debug logs

projectStructure.file: Process entry point. Boots the HTTP server, WebSocket server, and GameServer; wires graceful shutdown on SIGINT/SIGTERM.
type: module (ESM). No dependencies. "start" script runs node server.js.

directory.file: Central runtime constants: port, host, tick rate, max players, heartbeat timings.
Minimal timestamped console logger (info/warn/error/debug).
Dependency-free static file server for the client/ directory. MIME type map, path-traversal protection, 404/500 handling.
Hand-rolled RFC 6455 WebSocket server implementation (handshake via Sec-WebSocket-Accept, frame encode/decode, masking, text/ping/pong/close opcodes). No external ws library.
Shared message-type string constants for the client/server JSON protocol.

Connection manager: player registry, fixed-tick loop (setInterval at TICK_RATE_HZ), snapshot broadcasting, join/leave events, heartbeat ping loop. No gameplay/physics logic - players are static placeholders at (0,0,0).
Document shell: canvas, loading screen, debug HUD overlay. Title set to "Rise of Lyric".
Minimal CSS reset and fullscreen canvas layout only. No visual design/theming.
Client runtime constants (WS URL derivation, reconnect timing, camera FOV/near/far).
Tiny synchronous pub/sub EventBus used to decouple engine modules.
requestAnimationFrame game loop with delta-time clamping and rolling FPS calculation.
THREE.WebGLRenderer creation and window-resize handling.
THREE.PerspectiveCamera factory using core/config.js values.
Base scene: ambient + directional lights, ground plane, one placeholder rotating test cube, and a factory for remote-player placeholder meshes.
Keyboard key-state tracking, pointer-lock request on canvas click, raw mouse-delta accumulation. Records input only - no movement logic applied.

Browser WebSocket client wrapper: connect/reconnect with exponential backoff, JSON message parsing, dispatches events (net:connected, net:welcome, net:snapshot, net:playerJoin, net:playerLeave, net:disconnected) via the EventBus.
WorldState: holds latest snapshot of remote players (Map keyed by id) and the local player's id.
Loading-screen show/hide and debug overlay stat updates (FPS, ping, player count, connection status).

Bootstrap script. Wires renderer+scene+camera, input, network, world state, UI and the game loop together. Spawns/despawns placeholder boxes for remote players based on snapshots. Rotates a local test cube to prove the render loop is alive.
Three.js r160, vendored locally as an ES module (fetched from the official unpkg build). Imported directly by render/*.js via relative paths - no bundler/build step required.

clientToServer.message: Sent once after the socket opens. Fields: name.
Reserved for per-tick input state (keys, look angles). Currently stored but unused by simulation.
Heartbeat reply to a server ping.

serverToClient.message: Sent immediately on connect. Fields: id (assigned player id), tickRate.
Broadcast every tick. Fields: tick, players[] (id, name, x, y, z, ry).
Broadcast when a player connects. Fields: id, name.
Broadcast when a player disconnects. Fields: id.

implementedFeatures.feature: Dependency-free Node HTTP static file server with MIME types and path-traversal protection
Fixed-tick (20Hz) server game loop with player connection registry
JSON-based client/server protocol with join/leave/snapshot/heartbeat messages
Browser client bootstrap with Three.js scene, camera, renderer, resize handling
Input manager (keyboard state + pointer-lock mouse deltas), not yet applied to gameplay
World state registry synced from server snapshots; remote players rendered as placeholder boxes
Minimal debug HUD (FPS, ping placeholder, player count, connection status) and loading screen

notYetImplemented.item: Gameplay rules, combat, abilities, win/lose conditions
Visual design, art direction, models, textures, animations, sound
Matchmaking, rooms/lobbies beyond a single shared world
Real round-trip ping measurement (HUD field exists but is not wired to a timer yet)

verification.test: Verified raw TCP client completes RFC 6455 handshake (101 Switching Protocols) against server/websocket.js.
Verified client receives "welcome" on connect and continuous 20Hz "snapshot" messages reflecting the connected test player.
